newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Ex-Khmer Rouge leader may retire from politics.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Khmer Rouge leader may retire from politics.

text.p: Former top Khmer Rouge official Ieng Sary may step down as leader of the political movement he set up after splitting from rebel hardliners last year, an aide to Cambodia's first prime minister said.
"It's possible that, yes, the leadership will change inside the DNUM (Democratic National Union Movement) to the profit of Ei Chien," said Xavier D'Abzac, aide to Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Ei Chien is the former commander of the Khmer Rouge base at Pailin in northwestern Cambodia. A founder of the DNUM, he was recently appointed a major-general in the Cambodian army.
D'Abzac said no decision had yet been made, but added: "Ieng Sary said many times he is old and not in good health. It is possible he wants to retire and stop all political activity."

Ieng Sary, a foreign minister and deputy premier in the Khmer Rouge government during its 1975-79 "killing fields" rule, set up the DNUM with other rebel commanders after they split last August with rebel hardliners loyal to Pol Pot.

Ranariddh, of the royalist FUNCINPEC party, and his main partner and rival in the coalition government, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen of the Cambodian People's Party (CPP), have vied for the allegiance of thousands of recent defectors to the government side.

Ranariddh told reporters last week he had sounded out various political groups on joining an alliance called the Front Uni National (United National Front), and said the DNUM had agreed to the movement's charter and was expected to join.
Analysts said the DNUM's participation would be more palatable without Ieng Sary, seen as one of the architects of Khmer Rouge terror which left more than a million people dead.
King Norodom Sihanouk last September granted Ieng Sary amnesty from a death sentence handed down in absentia for his role in the Khmer Rouge regime.

The manager of the U.S.-funded Cambodian Genocide Programme said at the weekend enough evidence had been found over the past two years to "clearly implicate" Khmer Rouge leaders in crimes against humanity, including Ieng Sary.

The Khmer Rouge reneged on a 1991 U.N.-brokered peace pact and has been fighting the government formed after 1993 elections. The mass defections last year cost the group thousands of fighters, leaving a core of about 2,000 hardliners.
